# The map of packages/runner

One line per file, in what the file says of itself. The kinds of folder are in [README.md](../README.md).

## `docs/`

- [`what-a-run-writes.md`](../docs/what-a-run-writes.md): What a run writes

## `src/`

- [`chain-journey.ts`](../src/chain-journey.ts): The chain operations' journey through a world `world create` made (`./run.sh chain --world=<name>`): org.create founds northwind as dana, dana's and eli's signatures of the setup send it, a grant of manage-books to sam is proposed and executed the same way, and the chain is read back through the world's door after each landing.
- [`client.ts`](../src/client.ts): The scenarios' `Capxul` for one stage: the SDK's client (`Sdk.layer(Capxul)`) at the stage's two doors, with every call recorded for the checks.
- [`collector-env.entry.ts`](../src/collector-env.entry.ts): Entry, for a CI job's step (roadmap 4.7): finds the staging collector and mints the run's token from the shared state, as the runner does for itself (src/telemetry/export.ts, `collectorFound`), and hands them to the job's later steps through GitHub's `GITHUB_ENV` file, as OpenTelemetry's standard settings (OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_ENDPOINT, and OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_HEADERS with the token).
- [`door.ts`](../src/door.ts): The package's door.
- [`failure.ts`](../src/failure.ts): How the runner fails, and how a failure is worded in a run record: in the failure's own words, without stack frames (they name this machine's paths and say nothing about the world).
- [`given.ts`](../src/given.ts): What a scenario is handed as its starting world's facts (`Given`).
- [`in-world.ts`](../src/in-world.ts): A run in a world that `world create` made (`./run.sh door --world=<name>`), rather than in a stage of the runner's own: the same plan, the same calls and the same generic checks (run.ts), with the world's Core, its database and its tokens, read from the shared state of packages/world (world/existing.ts).
- [`main.ts`](../src/main.ts): Entry: `bun src/main.ts <command>`, through ../run.sh, which sets the environment; `USAGE` below lists every command and flag.
- [`record.ts`](../src/record.ts): What a run leaves behind once its stage is gone: one JSON file, written by the runner and never by hand, outside any world.
- [`run.ts`](../src/run.ts): Runs: for each one a fresh stage, the calls, the generic checks, a run record, and the stage's destruction.
- [`scenario-runs.ts`](../src/scenario-runs.ts): A run of the journeys in stages of `CapxulCore` (a run that expects Core's empty handlers), in one of two modes, ending in its summary (summary.ts).
- [`settings.ts`](../src/settings.ts): The runner's declared settings.
- [`steps.ts`](../src/steps.ts): What the runner hears of a journey's steps, and how it records them.
- [`summary-words.ts`](../src/summary-words.ts): What `passed` means for each kind of run, in words (a summary's `what`), and why a journey run against the empty handlers did not end as it must (summary.ts).
- [`summary.ts`](../src/summary.ts): The summary of a run of the journeys: one record whose `outcome` says whether every journey ended as the run expected, whether the run held every registered journey, and whether every stage it used is gone.
- [`timings.ts`](../src/timings.ts): Every part of a run in one world, timed in the order it happened (roadmap step 1.18; AGENTS.md, "Measure first"): the hub brought up, the world created, each starting world made, saved and kept on the bench, each reset before a journey, each journey's steps, the worlds a journey made destroyed, the world destroyed and the hub taken down.

## `src/checks/`

- [`checks.ts`](../src/checks/checks.ts): The generic checks, applied to every call of every run.
- [`events.ts`](../src/checks/events.ts): The generic `events` check.
- [`isolation.ts`](../src/checks/isolation.ts): The generic `isolation` check (roadmap step 4.8, "One shared world, every journey side by side"): every call of a journey acts only as the journey's own people and names no other journey's person, email or company.
- [`paths.ts`](../src/checks/paths.ts): The generic `path` check (docs/roadmap.md, "Lifecycles are machines in the blueprint", step 3.4).

## `src/local/`

- [`bundle.ts`](../src/local/bundle.ts): Core's Worker bundle for a local Core (`--core=local`): the same build Alchemy makes when it deploys Core to Cloudflare (its rolldown bundle of packages/core's Worker, wrapped in Alchemy's Worker bridge, with the compatibility date and flags a deploy gives it), written to a directory once per run, for workerd to serve.
- [`database.ts`](../src/local/database.ts): A local Core's way in to its world's database.
- [`forward.ts`](../src/local/forward.ts): A local Core's way to its world's chain and bundler.
- [`host.ts`](../src/local/host.ts): `--core=local`: every world the run makes gets its Core run here, in workerd, instead of as a Worker on Cloudflare (packages/world, src/core/host.ts).
- [`workerd.ts`](../src/local/workerd.ts): One world's local Core as a workerd process: Core's bundle (bundle.ts) served on a loopback port, with the bindings a deploy gives the Worker on Cloudflare (packages/world src/core/Core.ts), by the same names (CORE_ENV):  DATABASE   a Hyperdrive binding, as on Cloudflare, whose origin is the world's database bridge (database.ts) CHAIN      a service binding to the chain forwarder (forward.ts), which carries it to the world's door the rest   the world's facts and secrets as text, and the site door of the stand-in bench on this machine  workerd reads its configuration from a Cap'n Proto text file, written here with every secret in it; the file is in the run's own temporary directory, readable by this user only, and goes with it.

## `src/shared/`

- [`facts.ts`](../src/shared/facts.ts): What a shared world keeps of how its starting worlds were made: each one's facts (packages/blueprint, src/starting-points/facts.ts), as its maker answered them, in a table of the world's own database, written just before the snapshot of that starting world is saved.
- [`make.ts`](../src/shared/make.ts): `./run.sh shared`: makes the shared world, or renews it (roadmap step 2.3).
- [`starting.ts`](../src/shared/starting.ts): Starting worlds for a run on a shared world (roadmap steps 2.3 and 2.4): the same answers as the run's one world gives (worlds/starting.ts), but nothing is made in the shared world and it is never reset, because other callers use it.

## `src/telemetry/`

- [`export.ts`](../src/telemetry/export.ts): The runner's OTLP export (roadmap 4.4): the layer its entry (main.ts) provides once, so every span, log and metric it makes is posted over OTLP/HTTP JSON to the collector, under a resource naming the producer (`service.name`, the blueprint's producer) and the code's revision (`service.version`).
- [`flat.ts`](../src/telemetry/flat.ts): A decoded OTLP trace (otlp.ts) as flat spans: the shape the runner's checks read, in place of `app.spans`' columns (world/database.ts).
- [`logs.ts`](../src/telemetry/logs.ts): A decoded OTLP logs export (otlp.ts) as flat logs: what the tap holds of a call's logs, beside its flat spans (flat.ts).
- [`observe.ts`](../src/telemetry/observe.ts): What the runner observed of each call, by trace: its spans and logs from the tap (tap.ts) and the events Core recorded under its trace id (`app.events`).
- [`otlp.ts`](../src/telemetry/otlp.ts): OTLP JSON, as Effect's `OtlpSerialization.layerJson` writes it: the bodies of the trace, log and metric export requests (`/v1/traces`, `/v1/logs`, `/v1/metrics`).
- [`parity.ts`](../src/telemetry/parity.ts): Parity between the two records of one call's spans while both exist (roadmap 4.4, side by side): `app.spans`, which Core writes today (world/database.ts), and the tap, the same spans as OTLP (tap.ts, flat.ts).
- [`side-by-side.ts`](../src/telemetry/side-by-side.ts): Side by side (roadmap 4.4): for every call a run made through its own stage's door, the spans Core kept in `app.spans` beside the spans the tap holds of it (tap.ts), and their parity (parity.ts), for the run record.
- [`step.ts`](../src/telemetry/step.ts): A span the runner records under a name the blueprint declares (roadmap 4.7): its name from `Pipeline`, never written here as a string, and its kind under the envelope's `capxul.step.kind`.
- [`tap.ts`](../src/telemetry/tap.ts): The tap: in a test world, Core writes the OTLP it exports into the world's database as well (`telemetry.otlp`: the trace id, the signal, the body), and the runner reads a call's spans and logs back from it by trace id, through the same `/sql` endpoint it reads `app.spans` by (world/database.ts; roadmap 4.4; design note "Proof and telemetry", section 7).

## `src/world/`

- [`born.ts`](../src/world/born.ts): A stage's first record entry.
- [`database.ts`](../src/world/database.ts): The runner's way in to a stage's database: Neon's HTTPS SQL endpoint, the only way this container reaches Postgres (it has no TCP route out).
- [`existing.ts`](../src/world/existing.ts): A run against a world that `world create` made (packages/world), rather than a stage of `CapxulCore` of the runner's own: `./run.sh door --world=<name>`.
- [`leftovers.ts`](../src/world/leftovers.ts): What the accounts hold of one stage, read from Cloudflare's and Neon's own APIs by name: taken before a destroy, it proves the search finds the stage's resources; taken after, it shows nothing is left (roadmap, world lifecycle rule 4).
- [`stage.ts`](../src/world/stage.ts): The life of one stage of `CapxulCore` as a unit: create it, use it, report on it, destroy it, and look in the accounts afterwards.
- [`warmup.ts`](../src/world/warmup.ts): A new stage's address, while Cloudflare is still routing it (found by the pipeline spike: packages/core/docs/latency.md).

## `src/worlds/`

- [`company.ts`](../src/worlds/company.ts): The makers of the starting worlds with a company (packages/blueprint, src/things/company/verbs/create.ts, src/starting-points/points.ts, src/things/document/verbs/submit.ts, src/starting-points/facts.ts and src/common/site.ts; step 1.12): `founded`, `office-holder`, `payment-drafted`, `payment-held` and `paid`, each made by its declaration's steps (src/starting-points/points.ts) through the door of the world the steps run in, from the one before.
- [`encode.ts`](../src/worlds/encode.ts): How a starting world's maker keeps an answer as a fact: encoded as the blueprint's own schema of the operation encodes it (packages/blueprint, src/starting-points/facts.ts), so `given` decodes it with the same schema.
- [`ending.ts`](../src/worlds/ending.ts): The summary of a run in one world (run.ts), however it ended: a starting world that was not made, named by the part of it that failed, and a run that died go into its `oneWorld.failure`, which fails the run, so a run never ends without a summary that says why (PR #227's CI run 43599082569 died on a starting world's save and left no record at all).
- [`hub.ts`](../src/worlds/hub.ts): The fleet hub a run's one world lives on (packages/world, src/things/cluster; roadmap 1.15 and 1.18).
- [`journey-making.ts`](../src/worlds/journey-making.ts): Where the calls made for one journey's starting world go, and which journey it is (roadmap 4.8): provided per journey by the run (worlds/run.ts), read by the recorder (making.ts) and the makers (company.ts).
- [`kept.ts`](../src/worlds/kept.ts): What the platform this process serves kept of its calls (worlds/platform.ts): each call's spans, and the events it wrote into the record of the world it acted on.
- [`makers.ts`](../src/worlds/makers.ts): How the runner makes each starting world: by the steps its declaration names (packages/blueprint, src/starting-points/points.ts), each an operation through the door, from the world before it (packages/blueprint, src/starting-points/points.ts and src/starting-points/facts.ts).
- [`making.ts`](../src/worlds/making.ts): How a starting world's steps are run and recorded, whoever runs them: the run's one world (starting.ts) or a run on a shared world (shared.ts).
- [`places.ts`](../src/worlds/places.ts): How many worlds and company sites a run in one shared world has at once (roadmap 4.8 b; RUNNER_SHAPE=shared).
- [`platform.ts`](../src/worlds/platform.ts): The platform, served by this process for a run in private worlds (packages/blueprint, src/things/world/values.ts): the blueprint's platform group from packages/world, over HTTP on this machine's loopback, where the Cloudflare and Neon keys are.
- [`players.ts`](../src/worlds/players.ts): Who plays each role in a starting world with a company, and the keys they sign with (roadmap 4.8 with 4.11): the journey's own cast when the run casts every journey (`Casting`, a run in one shared world, side-by-side.ts), so journeys side by side never found the same company or share a person's Safe; otherwise each role by its own name.
- [`run.ts`](../src/worlds/run.ts): A run of the journeys in one world (`./run.sh scenarios`, expecting `pass`; roadmap step 1.18 and the decision "One runner, one world"): the platform served by this process (platform.ts), the run's hub brought up (hub.ts), its one world created on it and every starting world the journeys name made in it once and saved (starting.ts); then for each journey the world reset in place to its starting world, what that world makes by its steps made, the journey run through the door with its operations' checks and the generic checks on every call, and every other world it made destroyed after it, whatever happened, with the accounts read before and after for anything of them.
- [`side-by-side.ts`](../src/worlds/side-by-side.ts): A run with every journey at once in one shared world (RUNNER_SHAPE=shared; roadmap 4.8, decision D8).
- [`starting.ts`](../src/worlds/starting.ts): Starting worlds for a run in one world (roadmap step 1.18; docs/roadmap.md, "One runner, one world"; packages/blueprint, src/starting-points/points.ts).
- [`teardown.ts`](../src/worlds/teardown.ts): What a run in private worlds takes down, and what it reads of the accounts afterwards: the worlds it made, destroyed the newest first.
- [`timing.ts`](../src/worlds/timing.ts): `./run.sh starting-worlds`: makes every starting world the runner can make, in the blueprint's order, as a journey of it would get it, and times each: in the run's one world on its hub (worlds/hub.ts), each made once and saved, then for each the one world reset to it and what it makes by its steps made.
- [`wait.ts`](../src/worlds/wait.ts): The makers' wait for background work (decisions.md, 27): poll an operation until it answers differently.
